channel.title: AI Security Digest
channel.description: Curated AI security insights and articles from various sources

item.title: Introducing CodeMender: an AI agent for code security
item.description:
📄 Source: Google DeepMind Blog
👤 Author: DeepMind | 📅 Date: 2024-05-21
Artificial Intelligence Software Security Machine Learning
DeepMind has introduced CodeMender, an AI agent that autonomously detects and repairs security vulnerabilities in software code using advanced machine learning and reinforcement learning. Trained on extensive open-source code and patches, CodeMender effectively identifies and fixes issues like buffer overflows and injection flaws, outperforming existing automated tools and enhancing software security. The system aims to integrate into development workflows to support secure coding practices.

item.title: AI Threat Hunting: 4 Advantages of Automated Detection Systems
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 3, 2025
Cybersecurity Artificial Intelligence Threat Detection
Automated AI threat hunting leverages machine learning and automation to detect and respond to cyber threats targeting AI systems in real time, offering continuous monitoring and predictive analytics. This approach enhances threat intelligence, speeds up detection and response, provides 24/7 coverage, and reduces alert fatigue, making cybersecurity more effective against evolving AI-specific attacks.

item.title: AI Threat Intelligence: 4 Emerging Threats Facing AI Agents
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 3, 2025
AI Security Cybersecurity Threats Artificial Intelligence
AI agents face emerging threats such as memory poisoning, model extraction, identity spoofing, and multi-agent collusion that exploit their broad access, autonomy, and trust. Implementing AI threat intelligence solutions like adversarial attack simulations and automated incident responses is crucial for detecting, preventing, and mitigating these sophisticated attacks to protect critical business operations.

item.title: AI Threat Modeling: 5 Proven Strategies for Multi-Agent AI Systems
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 3, 2025
AI Security Multi-Agent Systems Threat Modeling
Multi-agent AI systems enhance efficiency by handling complex tasks but introduce unique security risks such as emergent behaviors, communication vulnerabilities, and escalation of threats. Proactive AI threat modeling using frameworks, automated tools, simulated attacks, guardrails, and continuous monitoring is essential to identify and mitigate these risks before they impact the system.

item.title: AI Threat Detection: 4 Best Practices to Stop Advanced Cyber Threats
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 3, 2025
Cybersecurity Artificial Intelligence Threat Detection
Attackers are increasingly using generative AI to conduct sophisticated, stealthy cyberattacks, prompting organizations to adopt AI-driven detection combined with diverse data sources, human oversight, and continuous retraining to improve resilience. While AI accelerates threat detection and response, challenges such as model manipulation and evolving attack tactics require a balanced approach integrating advanced tools and best practices.

item.title: What is Red Teaming in Cyber Security? The Complete Guide
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 3, 2025
Cybersecurity Ethical Hacking Risk Management
Red teaming is a proactive cybersecurity approach where ethical hackers simulate real-world attacks across technical, human, and physical vulnerabilities to identify and address security weaknesses before malicious actors exploit them. Unlike traditional penetration testing, red teaming takes a holistic and creative approach to uncover blind spots, making it applicable across various industries such as technology, finance, healthcare, government, and energy. This comprehensive strategy helps organizations improve defenses, test disaster response plans, and prepare for evolving cyber threats.

item.title: Mindgard Ups the Ante for Security of AI – Appoints Proven Cybersecurity Leader James Brear to Capture Expanding Market Opportunity
item.description:
📄 Source: MindGard Blog
👤 Author: Fergal Glynn | 📅 Date: October 6, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Security Cybersecurity Leadership Generative AI
Mindgard has appointed cybersecurity veteran James Brear as CEO and expanded its leadership team to accelerate growth in the generative AI cybersecurity market, projected to reach $35.5 billion by 2031. The company focuses on securing AI throughout its lifecycle by detecting shadow AI, automating red teaming, and ensuring runtime protection, with new U.S. headquarters in Boston to support expansion. Mindgard emphasizes offensive security principles to address emerging AI threats and ensure enterprise AI systems operate safely and compliantly.

item.title: NVIDIA’s Peter Belcak Distills Why Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Peter Belcak | 📅 Date: September 5, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Natural Language Processing Machine Learning Models
Peter Belcak from NVIDIA presents a paper arguing that small language models (SLMs) under 10 billion parameters are the future of agentic AI due to their efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for specialized tasks within heterogeneous systems. The approach involves using large models for planning and SLMs for repetitive or narrow tasks, enabling sustainable and reliable deployment of agentic systems.

Data Visualization Agent Engineering Experiment Management

item.title: Verizon’s Stan Miasnikov on His Paper: Category Theoretic Analysis of Inter-Agent Communication and Mutual Understanding Metric in Recursive Consciousness
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: David Burch | 📅 Date: September 6, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Category Theory Inter-Agent Communication
Stan Miasnikov of Verizon presented his recent paper on extending a recursive consciousness framework using category theory to analyze inter-agent communication and quantify the loss of meaning during translation. The work aims to deepen understanding of mutual comprehension metrics among AI agents. This was featured in an Arize community AI research paper reading session.

item.title: Building a Multilingual Cypher Query Evaluation Pipeline
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
📅 Date: September 9, 2025
Multilingual AI Natural Language Processing Database Query Generation
The article discusses building a multilingual evaluation pipeline to test large language models' ability to generate accurate Cypher queries from non-English business questions. Using Phoenix for observability and open source translation tools, the pipeline translates English queries into languages like Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu, then assesses the syntactic and semantic correctness of generated queries against English ground truth. This approach enables iterative improvements and reliable multilingual AI-driven database querying.

item.title: Orchestrator & Worker Agents: A Practical Comparison of Common Agent Frameworks
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Sanjana Yeddula, Aparna Dhinakaran, Sri Chavali | 📅 Date: September 9, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Agent Frameworks Workflow Orchestration
The article provides a technical analysis of the orchestrator-worker agent architecture, highlighting its dynamic and multi-stage reasoning workflow where an orchestrator decomposes user input into subtasks assigned to specialized worker agents. It compares leading frameworks such as Agno, Autogen, CrewAI, OpenAI, LangGraph, and Mastra, discussing their approaches, strengths, and challenges in implementing this pattern. Key challenges include dynamic routing, task complexity management, and maintaining evolving task states.

item.title: ADB Benchmarks
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Jason Lopatecki | 📅 Date: September 17, 2025
Database Performance Benchmarking Real-time Data Processing
The article presents benchmark tests for adb (Arize database), evaluating its performance both as a database and within an application context. Tests include dataset upload speed, real-time trace ingestion, and full-text search efficiency over large datasets, demonstrating adb's capability for fast data ingestion and responsive user experience under specified network conditions.

item.title: Rise of the Agent Engineer: Trunk Tools — Bobby Vinson
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Bobby Vinson | 📅 Date: September 19, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Construction Technology Data Management
Trunk Tools is revolutionizing the $13 trillion construction industry by leveraging AI agents to streamline data management, automate repetitive tasks, and reduce waste. Bobby Vinson, an AI Evaluation Engineer at Trunk Tools, discusses their development of specialized AI agents that assist construction teams in accessing timely information and maintaining project coordination, emphasizing the importance of best practices and thorough evaluation in complex AI systems.

item.title: Atropos Health’s Arjun Mukerji, PhD, Explains RWEsummary: A Framework and Test for Choosing LLMs to Summarize Real-World Evidence (RWE) Studies
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Arjun Mukerji, PhD | 📅 Date: September 19, 2025
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Natural Language Processing Real-World Evidence
Arjun Mukerji, PhD from Atropos Health introduces RWESummary, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on their ability to accurately summarize structured real-world evidence (RWE) studies in healthcare. The framework prioritizes critical evaluation criteria such as direction of effect, numerical accuracy, and completeness to ensure safe and reliable AI application in high-stakes medical decision-making. Results show trade-offs between model accuracy and speed, underscoring the need for domain-specific benchmarks to improve LLM performance in medicine.

item.title: Testing Binary vs Score LLM Evals on the Latest Models
item.description:
📄 Source: Arize Blog
👤 Author: Aparna Dhinakaran, Co-founder & Chief Product Officer & Sri Chavali, AI Engineer | 📅 Date: September 24, 2025
Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models Model Evaluation
The article examines the effectiveness of binary versus score-based evaluation methods for assessing large language model (LLM) outputs, comparing results from 2024 and retesting with newer models in 2025. Findings indicate that binary evaluations tend to yield more consistent and reliable results than score-based approaches, which often produce plateaued or bimodal distributions. The study tests various scoring rubrics and corruption types, ultimately recommending best practices for LLM evaluation formats.
